newsitem.title: USA: Economists divided on whether Fed will intervene.
newsitem.headline: Economists divided on whether Fed will intervene.

text.p: Economists were divided as to whether the Federal Reserve would intervene by injecting reserves into the money system Wednesday or remain on the sidelines.

Economists at MMS International said the Fed had adequately addressed its add need with term repurchase agreements put on the books already in the current two-week maintenance period and thus could remain out of the banking system Wednesday.

Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, said that with federal funds currently trading right at the Fed's official target level of 5.25 percent, she thought the Fed would stay out of the system.

But Marc Wanshel, economist at J.P. Morgan & Co, expected the Fed would replace the $6.5 billion six-day term RP arranged last Thursday with a substantially smaller operation -- most likely a five-day fixed RP of between $2 billion to $3 billion.
The Federal Reserve added reserves into the banking system on Monday via 9-day system repurchase agreements.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663 ))
